guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 authorization-code authorization for apps that act for individual user accounts. The default read scope covers read access to the authorizing user's account, so it is the least-privilege documented grant for reading issue titles. Cursor pagination is documented separately. Write scopes are not needed and are excluded. App registration, redirect configuration and per-workspace consent are setup requirements that must be completed before the first test.

findings.title: OAuth2 authorization code flow is documented for per-user access
findings.detail: Linear supports OAuth2 and recommends it for applications integrating with Linear. Per-user authorization uses actor=user, which is the default and creates or reads resources as the user who authorized the application, matching individual customer account authorization.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer authorizes their own Linear account through the OAuth flow.

findings.title: Create the OAuth2 application and configure redirect URIs before testing
findings.detail: The OAuth2 application must be created in Linear with redirect callback URLs configured for the app. Linear recommends creating a dedicated workspace to manage the application because each admin user gains access to it. Client credentials and redirect configuration are required before the first authorization test.

findings.title: Access tokens expire after 24 hours and require refresh
findings.detail: A successful token exchange returns an access token valid for 24 hours plus a refresh token. Refresh tokens must be used to obtain new access tokens when the previous one expires, so per-customer token storage and refresh handling are required.
findings.appliesWhen: Ongoing reads for each connected customer account after authorization.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles from the connected workspace
steps.detail: Call the GraphQL endpoint with the bearer access token, requesting the first 10 issues with pageInfo. Titles are read only; no mutation is sent.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains issue title nodes plus pageInfo.hasNextPage and pageInfo.endCursor. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: ```graphql query Issues {
hasNextPage endCursor } }
``` Or pass the token as an authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues { issues(first: 10) { edges { node { id title } cursor } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: obtained from the token exchange step for the test account

steps.title: Verify read-only boundary using the granted scope and request log
steps.detail: Confirm the access token's scope is read only and inspect the outgoing request log to confirm only query operations were sent. Do not send any mutation to test enforcement.
steps.doneWhen: The token response scope is read and the request log shows no issueCreate, issueUpdate or delete operations.

evidence.quote: * `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.
* `issues:create` - Allows creating and updating issues, and creating their attachments

fields: scope: value returned in the token response

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles using the returned endCursor
steps.detail: Repeat the same query with after set to pageInfo.endCursor from the prior response. Continue while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true; stop when it is false.
steps.doneWhen: hasNextPage returns false and all pages are collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues($after: String) { issues(first: 10, after: $after) { edges { node { id title } cursor } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }","variables":{"after":"<END_CURSOR_FROM_PREVIOUS_RESPONSE>"}}'

fields: after: pageInfo.endCursor from the prior GraphQL response for the same query
ACCESS_TOKEN: same token used for the first page
